{{Short description|American mathematician}}
'''William H. Bossert''' (born 1937) is an American mathematician. He is the David B. Arnold, Jr. Professor of Science, Emeritus at [[Harvard University]]. He was the housemaster of [[Lowell House]] for 23 years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/04/15/us/harvard-breaks-a-housemaster-mold.html|title=Harvard Breaks a Housemaster Mold|first=Julie|last=Flaherty|work=The New York Times |date=April 15, 1998|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.seas.harvard.edu/person/william-bossert|title=William H. Bossert &#124; Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences|website=www.seas.harvard.edu}}</ref>  He received his PhD from Harvard in 1963.<ref>{{Cite web|title=William Bossert - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=18745|access-date=2021-12-31|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

==Publications==
